text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Association of depositors of the bankrupt TAT pyramid savings scheme dissatisfied because the National Bank of Macedonia did not include the savings society's general manager Sonja Nikolovska, now in custody, in the probe of TAT's financial documentation.
- Association of private pharmacies and several prominent Macedonian doctors believe Minister Ilija Filipce is responsible for the chaotic situation in the country's health services and must resign.
- The Macedonian government is still considering wether or not to send Macedonian soldiers to participate in the international operation Alba in Albania.
- Most farms in Macedonia have not met their dues towards factories that produce cattle fodder, which is the reason for the pestilence among several hundred animals a few days ago.
- Since the adoption of the Law on Citizenship, only 521 out of 118,508 requests for citizeship have been refused, said Interior Minister Tomislav Cokrevski.
- Leader of ethnic Albanian PDPA party Arben Dzaferi accuses Macedonian police of detaining and beating its activists.

- Skopje refinery Okta owes the state $17 million in unpaid taxes. The management of the refinery calls on government assistance to overcome debt problems. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
